statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative-template audit. Radar rendering did not expose map content in headless Chrome, so map-specific usability was not asserted; all atomic checks were nevertheless judged with other direct evidence.

page.notes: Public, locale-aware weather forecast MPA/hybrid with forecast listings, interactive radar, account flow, advertising and consent management. Not covered: signup/password recovery, geolocation permission flow, paid/commercial flows, individual editorial articles, every locale, or live field INP.

paths.description: Landing/current-conditions forecast and global navigation; representative forecast overview.
Hourly forecast listing, representing dense time-series weather content.
Ten-day forecast listing and repeated long-page scroll interaction.
Interactive radar entry, representing the map-heavy journey.
Account sign-in form, representing authentication and form handling.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: Screenshots under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark are visually identical: the consent surface and page remain fixed light/white, and the DOM probe found no site dark-theme response.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Forecast route and state changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The comprehensive CSS probe found no view-transition rules even though daily, hourly, 10-day and radar are prominent state/route changes.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-document or cross-document View Transitions for forecast navigation, with a reduced-motion fallback.

findings.summary: Long forecast pages do not expose scroll-state-aware chrome.
findings.evidence: The DOM/CSS probe found no scroll timeline and the long hourly/10-day templates expose no progress or scroll-aware header state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a sticky header plus scroll-state/container-query or progress treatment that preserves location context.

findings.summary: Menus and overlays are not built with CSS anchor positioning.
findings.evidence: The page contains menu/dialog surfaces, while the CSS probe found no anchor-name, position-anchor, or position-try rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Use popover plus CSS anchor positioning and position-try fallbacks for menus and transient overlays.

findings.summary: A first-visit consent dialog obscures the entire forecast until a choice is made.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile load screenshots show a blocking cookie dialog covering the primary weather content; on mobile it consumes nearly the full viewport. Reject all is equally prominent, which avoids a deceptive-choice finding.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise the initial notice, preserve equal accept/reject choices, and avoid obscuring the primary forecast where consent law permits.

findings.summary: Advertising and sponsored chrome repeatedly interrupt forecast content.
findings.evidence: Rendered today/10-day DOM includes repeated “Advertisement” slots and “Sponsored Content”; the HAR records 78 third-party requests, while core forecast pages devote substantial structure to non-content modules.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce ad-slot frequency and reserve quieter, clearly separated placements after core forecast content.

findings.summary: Lab loading performance misses the Core Web Vitals quality bar.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.7 s, CLS 0.146 and TBT 530 ms (performance 45). The first-party trace was better at LCP 2.29 s and TBT 91.5 ms, showing variability but not negating the poor throttled result.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP chain, prioritise the hero background, remove redirects, and defer non-critical ad/analytics work.

findings.summary: Late forecast content causes measurable layout shift.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured CLS 0.146, including a 0.135 shift from an animated skeleton; the narrow layout probes were stable after their observation window.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve final component geometry for forecast skeletons and media; do not replace placeholders with differently sized content.

findings.summary: JavaScript keeps the main thread busy during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 3.4 s main-thread work, 2.3 s JavaScript execution, and 530 ms TBT; the trace also captured a 141.5 ms long task.
findings.suggestedFix: Split and defer forecast-independent code, schedule lower-priority work, and delay ads/analytics until after core content is interactive.

findings.summary: The landing page ships a heavy, redirecting critical path.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 143 requests and 2.42 MB transferred, including two document redirects and multiple parser-discovered high-priority scripts; Lighthouse estimates 850 ms redirect waste and reports a 12.7 s LCP without fetchpriority.
findings.suggestedFix: Link directly to the resolved locale/location URL, prioritise the LCP image, and move non-critical scripts off the critical path.

findings.summary: Large unused and legacy JavaScript dominates transfer cost.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 779 KiB unused JavaScript and 76 KiB legacy JavaScript. HAR shows 62 scripts and 2.09 MB script transfer, led by Taboola, Google Ads and Rubicon.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load advertising, identity and analytics bundles after consent/intent; remove legacy transforms for modern browsers.

findings.summary: Some interactive controls have incomplete or mismatched accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse details multiple hourly links whose aria-label omits visible label content, and the DOM probe found five links plus several buttons with no text or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Make each accessible name include the visible time/temperature label and label icon-only links/buttons explicitly.

findings.summary: The page logs runtime and hydration errors during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse captured React hydration error #418, FedCM NetworkError and missing en-GB translation messages in the console.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix server/client markup divergence, guard FedCM failures, and supply all en-GB message keys without logging production errors.

findings.summary: Production debugging and asset hygiene is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found a large first-party JavaScript chunk without a source map and 24 KiB minification savings.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish correct production source maps to an authenticated error pipeline and fully minify shipped bundles.

findings.summary: Some crawlable links use non-descriptive text.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO found the hourly link text “More”; the DOM also includes empty links. The viewport and real hrefs otherwise passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace generic labels with destination-specific text such as “View full hourly forecast” and label logo/social links.

findings.summary: One hreflang entry is invalid.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports hreflang="xc-MN" as an unexpected language code. Canonical, robots and sitemap signals were otherwise present and successful.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate only valid BCP 47 hreflang values and validate the locale map before deployment.

findings.summary: Core browser security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: Headers probe found no CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy; clickjacking protection was absent. Cookie probe found 15 cookies flagged insecure and extensive SameSite=None use. HTTPS and HSTS passed.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash CSP, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy and a minimal Permissions-Policy; mark every HTTPS cookie Secure and narrow SameSite.

findings.summary: The default page load has a large advertising and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker probe found 16 third-party origins and eight known trackers. HAR attributed 78 requests and 1.40 MB to third parties, including Taboola, DoubleClick, Rubicon and Amazon Ads.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate non-essential vendors on consent, reduce the vendor set, batch analytics, and load third parties only where they provide visible user value.

findings.summary: Sign-in exposes password-only authentication with no observed passkey path.
findings.evidence: The login DOM contains email/password controls and no WebAuthn/passkey affordance; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Add passkey registration/authentication and retain password recovery as a fallback.

findings.summary: The app-like weather experience has no active offline runtime.
findings.evidence: A web app manifest exists, but the runtime probe found no controlling service worker; forecast access therefore has no demonstrated offline fallback.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a service worker with a lightweight offline shell and cache the last successful forecast with clear staleness messaging.

findings.summary: The sign-in fields omit standard autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: Login DOM shows both email and password inputs with empty autocomplete attributes; the site-search input explicitly uses autocomplete="off".
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete="username" and autocomplete="current-password"; keep search suggestions separate from browser autofill.

findings.summary: A footer raster image is oversized and inefficient.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports the 256×256 Storm Radar PNG displayed around 70×70, with about 41 KiB potential savings; the image probe confirms a legacy PNG among otherwise SVG assets.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve an appropriately sized AVIF/WebP (or SVG where possible) with responsive variants.

findings.summary: Third-party script cost is disproportionate to the core forecast task.
findings.evidence: HAR reports 1.40 MB third-party transfer across 78 requests; the largest scripts are recommendation and ad systems, while Lighthouse identifies their bundles as mostly unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, remove low-value vendors, and defer the remainder until consent and visible need.
